title: Trophäen – Geweihe und Hörner (Trophies – Antlers and Horns)

details.heading: Grundbegriffe (Basic terms)
facts: Geweih (antlers): trophy of Rotwild (red deer), Rehwild (roe deer), and Damwild (fallow deer).
Rosen (antler coronets): present on mature deer antlers; distinguish from Rosenstock (pedicle).
Rosenstock (pedicle): the bony antler base; its thickness and shape are discussed in roe deer age assessment.

details.heading: Rotwild (Red deer)
facts: Mittelsprosse (middle tine): a reference point in the antler terminology.
Eissprosse (bez tine): often absent according to the class slides.
Krone (crown): the class describes three or more points above the Mittelsprosse.
Rosen (coronets) and Rosenstock (pedicle): used in class antler development and age discussions.

details.heading: Rehwild (Roe deer)
facts: Stangen (beams) and Enden (tines): length and mass are discussed in antler development.
Perlen (pearling) and Rosen (coronets): visible antler features.
Sechser (six-pointer): may already occur in the first year.
Rosenstock (pedicle): its thickness is an age-related indicator in the slides.
Peak antler development is given as about five to six years.

details.heading: Damwild (Fallow deer)
facts: Schaufeln (palms): broad palmated sections of developed fallow deer antlers.
Young stags initially grow spikes without Rosen (coronets); later antlers develop coronets and may form Schaufeln (palms).

details.heading: Muffelwild (Mouflon)
facts: The class covers abnormal or poor horn growth.

otherFacts: The class connects trophy and antler development with species recognition and age assessment.
Trophy Part 1 lists Geweih (antlers) and horns among possible trophies and explains preservation choices.
Trophy Part 2 covers European skull mounts; protect Rosen (coronets) during cooking and whitening.
No numerical CIC trophy scoring thresholds were found in the two Trophy Preparation decks reviewed; do not invent scoring formulas or trophy grades.
